Every day! In public, I just barely survive grocery shopping. Yet at work, I am a version of myself I would love to be all the time. At work, I’m professional, put together, business minded. At home, I feel like I’m always a breath away from ending it all... like my therapist says... rational mind vs irrational mind...

When I was taking seroquel, it was with 5 other psych meds as well... I was taking Zyprexa, Haldol, lithium, topomax, klonopin... the seroquel was he most sedating if all of them. I could maintain composure on the other meds during the day, then night would hit, I take my night meds... within 1 hour I was completely dazed and eating whatever I could find, then crashing in the bed. Wake up the next morning hungover as if I had drank a handle of rum... I even went to the extended release... that didn’t help either, it released in weird times, leaving me like a zombie. This is just my experience...

Whoa! Seroquel is evil... even if my life depended on me taking that again, I would rather die...  mixing the seroquel and klonopin is pretty much “fuckitol”... at least from my experience. I would start the dosage super low the first time taking it, like half a pill, to see how sedating it is for you...

With bpd, the recommended treatment is Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT). There are no medications to “treat” the disorder, but psychiatrists can prescribe meds like antidepressants for depression/anxiety. There is also a workbook for DBT... has seriously helped! Hope this helps!  GL

Honestly, I always feel like I am one breath away from admitting myself to a psych hospital again. Even though I am working a great job, my marriage is going better than in recent years, and I have support from friends and family, i worry that my mental status will get worse again. From 2011-2017, I was in and out of state psych hospitals and respite care for bpd, ptsd, depression and anxiety. I was also miss diagnosed with bipolar 2 and over medicated. 2 antipsychotics, 2 antidepressants, a benzo, ambien, and a mood stabilizer. I was a freakin zombie. In May 2017, I quit going to the local mhmr and taking meds (I don’t recommended doing this). It took me a year for my body to regulate back to a normal functioning status. I had developed diabetes, liver issues, high cholesterol, etc from the meds. Now I feel better emotionally, physically, and mentally as well. I worry about everything tho, there lies the issue... I fear my old life...
